questions.question: What does the self-attention mechanism let each token in a transformer do?
options: Only look at the single word immediately before it
Directly look at and weigh the relevance of every other token in the input, all at once
Ignore all other tokens and process independently
Only look at tokens that share the exact same spelling
questions.explanation: Self-attention lets every token compute a relevance weight for every other token, allowing the model to build a context-aware representation regardless of distance between related words.

questions.question: Why does doubling an LLM's context length roughly quadruple attention computation, rather than just doubling it?
options: It doesn't — attention cost scales linearly with input length
Because every token attends to every other token, so computation scales with the square (N x N) of input length
Because the model has to be retrained from scratch for longer inputs
Because longer inputs require more GPUs regardless of the model architecture
questions.explanation: Since attention requires each of N tokens to compute a relevance score against every other token, total computation scales roughly with N squared, so doubling N roughly quadruples the work.

questions.question: A team wants to double a chatbot's context window and assumes cost will roughly double. Which question best corrects this assumption?
options: Can we just accept whatever cost happens without checking?
Given attention's quadratic scaling, has the actual cost/latency increase been benchmarked, rather than estimated as a simple linear doubling?
Why does the model need attention at all?
Can we remove attention to make the model cheaper?
questions.explanation: Because attention computation scales quadratically with input length, doubling context length is expected to roughly quadruple attention cost, not simply double it — this should be benchmarked rather than assumed linear.
